title: The Digital CS Follow-up Check
subtitle: See who received your digital journey, who acted, who went quiet, and what to do next.
intro_text: Use this worksheet for one digital segment. Record what the system sent, what the customer did, what remains unknown, and when a person should step in. This is a follow-up check, not a retention prediction.
scoring_note: Do not turn this check into another universal score. Use it to find missing information, quiet customers, and follow-up that nobody owns.
closing_quote: Automation earns the word coverage only when the team can see silence and knows what to do next.
next_action: Choose one digital segment and inspect the last complete customer cycle. Find one account where delivery was recorded but nobody knows what the customer did next. Assign the follow-up and a review date.
interpretation: The customer completed a meaningful next action

sections.title: What should this programme help the customer do?
sections.why_it_matters: A send is not useful until the team names the customer decision or behaviour it is intended to change.
sections.review_prompt: What customer movement should this programme create, and how would the team recognise it?
rows: The problem the programme helps the customer complete
The decision or behaviour expected next
When the team will inspect the result

sections.title: Who received it, and what did they do?
sections.why_it_matters: Delivery, opening, responding, and changing behaviour are different events. Combining them hides uncertainty.
sections.review_prompt: Which accounts were technically reached but still produced no useful evidence?
rows: Accounts and contacts that should receive the programme
Reply, click, attendance, request, or other response
Do not treat an open as intent
The intended customer action or decision occurred

sections.title: When should a person step in?
sections.why_it_matters: A quiet customer only becomes useful information when the team agrees when to follow up, who will do it, and what a helpful response looks like.
sections.review_prompt: When should this stop being an automated journey and become a human follow-up?
rows: The response or customer progress the team expected
The event or amount of time that means someone should check
What returns the account to the digital journey

sections.title: What did we learn?
sections.why_it_matters: The programme should become more useful because the team can inspect what changed, not because more activity was sent.
sections.review_prompt: What did this cycle teach the team about the segment, message, trigger, or human response?
rows: What weakens the current programme theory
